title: 4.2. Returning Data, Recursion & Mathematical Functions
summary: Send results back to callers using return, explore the None value, write pure functions, and implement recursive algorithms.
learningObjectives: Use return expressions to pass computed values back to callers.
Understand what None represents when a function does not return explicitly.
Construct recursive functions with explicit base cases to avoid RecursionError.

sections.heading: 4.2.1 The return Statement and None
sections.content: The return statement terminates function execution immediately and optionally sends a value back to the caller. If a function reaches the end of its body without executing a return, it implicitly returns None.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: What does a Python function return by default if no return statement is specified?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: Functions lacking an explicit return return the special None value.

recap: return yields results and exits functions; non-returning functions return None.
